Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the InnovaTech Q3 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today’s call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Sarah Chen, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Sarah Chen, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to InnovaTech’s Q3 earnings call. With me today are Dr. Anya Sharma, CEO; David Lee, CFO; Michael Brown, COO; and Dr. Kenji Tanaka, CTO.
Earlier today, we published our press release and earnings slides, which are available on our IR website. Please note that this call may contain forward-looking statements. With that, I’ll turn it over to Dr. Sharma.

Dr. Anya Sharma, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Sarah, and welcome, everyone.

We had a strong quarter with performance driven by several key initiatives. First, I’d like to address our gross margin performance, which reflects our continued execution on core growth priorities. Our Q3 2024 gross profit reached $28.7 billion, a slight decrease from Q2 2024's $30.9 billion, resulting in a gross margin of 42.3%, a 2.7 percentage point decline sequentially. This was largely anticipated, given the market dynamics, which I'll elaborate on. The sequential decrease in gross profit and margin is primarily due to price erosion in our memory segment, specifically DRAM and NAND flash. We saw an average selling price decline of approximately 18% in DRAM and 22% in NAND flash during the quarter. This stems from an industry-wide oversupply, weaker demand in the PC and mobile sectors earlier this year, and aggressive pricing strategies from competitors, particularly those based in China aiming to increase market share in specific DRAM and NAND tiers. There was also a slight shift in our product mix towards lower-margin, higher-volume memory solutions as some customers prioritized cost optimization. For example, server DRAM sales saw a modest decline of about 5% sequentially as data center buildouts slowed. Offsetting these factors somewhat, we saw a 12% increase in overall DRAM unit shipments and a 15% increase in NAND unit shipments due to strategic customer engagements and promotions. Our cost reduction initiatives, especially in advanced packaging and manufacturing process optimization, yielded around $700 million in savings. This includes the successful ramp-up of our 1alpha DRAM node with improved cost efficiencies. Our non-memory segments, including Foundry and System LSI, performed well, with the Foundry business seeing a 10% revenue increase sequentially due to strong demand for leading-edge process technologies from HPC and automotive customers. Year-over-year, the gross margin picture is more pronounced with our Q3 2024 gross margin of 42.3% significantly lower than the 49.8% in Q3 2023, a 7.5 percentage point decline. This reflects a YoY ASP decline in DRAM and NAND estimated at 35% and 40%, respectively, reflecting the continued oversupply and competitive pricing. Increased trade tensions and technology export restrictions have also contributed to market volatility, especially in the Chinese market, leading to demand shifts. While we've mitigated cost increases, inflationary pressures on raw materials, energy, and logistics continue to impact our cost structure. During our Q2 call, we guided for a gross margin of 44% to 46% for Q3. The shortfall was primarily due to a greater-than-anticipated decline in memory ASPs, a slower-than-expected demand recovery, and unfavorable currency fluctuations, particularly the strengthening of the Korean Won against the US Dollar. We're now accelerating efforts to shift towards higher-value, higher-margin memory solutions, such as high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI applications and enterprise-grade SSDs, with HBM sales expected to represent a significantly larger portion of our revenue in 2025 and beyond. We’re also committed to technology leadership in memory and process technology, with the successful ramp-up of our 1beta DRAM node and next-generation NAND technology being crucial for cost competitiveness and product differentiation. Diversifying our revenue streams through our Foundry and System LSI businesses will also help, as will intensifying our focus on operational efficiency and cost reduction. Looking ahead to Q4, we anticipate a more stable pricing environment in the memory market, with some potential for a modest price rebound. We expect our Q4 gross margin to be in the range of 43% to 45%, reflecting the benefits of our strategic initiatives and a slightly improved pricing environment.

We also made meaningful progress with key areas within our System LSI, Foundry, and Display segments. We anticipate a strong performance in the System LSI division, projecting revenue to reach $5.8 billion in Q3, a 12% increase quarter-over-quarter and a 7% increase year-over-year. This growth is primarily due to the expected success of a new flagship smartphone launch by one of our key tier-one Android partners. We forecast a 22% QoQ increase in SoC revenue, reaching $3.1 billion in Q3, based on securing significant orders for our Exynos 2400 series SoC designed for this flagship device. We project 18 million unit sales globally for that partner’s device in Q3, directly translating to higher SoC demand. We've also made strategic pricing adjustments, offering volume discounts to maintain market share and secure long-term partnerships. However, we anticipate a slight decline (approximately 3%) in our image sensor business due to increased competition, particularly in the mid-range smartphone market. We are actively working on next-generation image sensor technology to regain market share, with positive revenue impacts anticipated in Q4. We expect the strongest SoC demand to originate from North America and Europe, aligning with the projected sales distribution of our partner’s device, with moderate growth in emerging markets due to price sensitivity. For the full year, we are revising our initial System LSI revenue growth forecast upward to 6%, reflecting the strong Q3 performance, but remain cautiously optimistic about Q4 due to the cyclical nature of the smartphone market. We are accelerating R&D efforts to diversify our product portfolio beyond mobile SoCs, targeting automotive and AI applications. Our Foundry business is poised for substantial growth in Q3, with revenue projected to increase by 18% QoQ, reaching $7.5 billion, driven by robust demand across various applications and our ability to maximize production capacity. We are seeing increased demand from High-Performance Computing (HPC), automotive, and 5G infrastructure sectors. We anticipate a 25% increase in automotive-related revenue in Q3. The proportion of revenue generated from advanced nodes (5nm and below) is expected to increase to 45% in Q3, up from 38% in Q2, driving higher ASPs and improved profitability. We have implemented initiatives to optimize our production capacity, increasing our fab utilization rate to 95% in Q3. We anticipate the most significant growth to come from North America and Asia-Pacific, driven by the concentration of HPC and automotive customers. We are maintaining our full-year revenue growth forecast for the Foundry business at 25%, reflecting our confidence in our ability to capitalize on long-term trends. We are investing heavily in expanding our production capacity, including new fabs in the US and South Korea, and anticipate being ready for 3nm mass production by Q4. In the Display segment, in a challenging environment, Samsung Display aims to maintain earnings growth quarter-over-quarter by leveraging competitive advantages in the high-end market and capitalizing on favorable exchange rates. We project a 3% QoQ revenue increase, reaching $8.2 billion, focusing on the high-end market with premium OLED displays, including foldable displays. We anticipate a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion from sales of foldable OLED panels. The weakening of the Korean Won against the US dollar is providing a tailwind, and we project a positive $150 million impact to net profit due to exchange rate fluctuations. We are working closely with key customers to develop customized display solutions and continuing to ramp up production of our QD-OLED displays for TVs. We are cautiously optimistic about the full-year outlook for the Display business, expecting continued growth in the high-end market, but are mindful of potential economic headwinds. We expect growth to be relatively flat for the full year, with revenue up only 1% compared to the previous year, and are investing $3 billion in R&D over the next three years to drive innovation.

On a broader level, our net margin and diluted EPS performance supported our positioning. The Board has approved a quarterly dividend of $0.36 per share for both common and preferred stock, aligning with our stated dividend policy and reflecting our commitment to returning value to shareholders. Based on the current policy and share count, the total quarterly payout will be $2.45 trillion, scheduled for mid-November disbursement. The Board’s decision reflects confidence in our sustained profitability and cash flow generation, with our current payout ratio at a comfortable 38% of net income, allowing for continued investment in growth initiatives. In Q3 2024, we achieved a net margin of 12.7%, a slight improvement of 0.5 percentage points compared to Q3 2023 (12.2%) and a 0.2 percentage point increase from Q2 2024 (12.5%). This improvement is significant considering headwinds like rising raw material costs and increased competition. This net margin expansion was driven by operational efficiency gains from our "Smart Factory 2.0" initiative, resulting in a 3.5% reduction in production costs across our Korean and Vietnamese plants, and a successful shift towards higher-margin premium offerings, particularly in our consumer electronics division with the launch of new OLED televisions with integrated AI capabilities, boosting our average selling price (ASP). For example, sales of our premium TVs in North America saw a 22% increase compared to Q3 2023. However, increased marketing expenses for new product launches and currency fluctuations, specifically the weakening of the Korean Won, negatively impacted our reported net margin by approximately 0.3 percentage points. Our diluted earnings per share (EPS) for Q3 2024 came in at $1.75, representing an 8% increase compared to $1.62 in Q3 2023, correlating to the improvement in our net margin and overall increase in net income. This is slightly below our initial projections of 10% due to the aforementioned currency headwinds and increased marketing spend. Key drivers of the EPS growth include a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion, driven by our expansion into emerging markets in Southeast Asia, and our ongoing share repurchase program, having repurchased approximately 2 million shares during Q3. However, our EPS growth was also impacted by increased interest expenses associated with our recent bond issuance to finance our expansion plans in the renewable energy sector. From a regional perspective, our performance varied significantly, with North America and Europe showing strong growth in the premium segment, while emerging markets in Asia and Latin America drove volume growth in our mid-range products. China remains a competitive market, and we are actively adapting our strategy. Looking ahead, we are focused on several key strategic initiatives to further improve our net margin and EPS, including continued investment in R&D (earmarking $5 trillion for the next fiscal year), supply chain optimization, and digital transformation.

I’ll now hand it over to David Lee to walk you through the financials.

David Lee, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Dr. Sharma, and hello, everyone.

This quarter’s financial results were underpinned by operational rigor and discipline. Let’s walk through the key metrics.

To start, proactive cost-cutting measures across the organization helped to mitigate the impact of the Memory business downturn helped drive improvements in our operating margin. Our total CapEx for Q3 landed at $12.7 trillion, reflecting our strategic investments in key growth areas. The cumulative CapEx for the year-to-date period, ending Q3, reached $33 trillion, putting us slightly ahead of our initial projected budget of $32 trillion, primarily driven by accelerated investments in our DS division. As anticipated, the DS division accounted for the majority of our CapEx in Q3, consuming $11.5 trillion. This brings the year-to-date investment in DS to $29.1 trillion. This significant allocation underscores our commitment to maintaining a technological edge in the semiconductor market. A substantial portion of the DS CapEx, approximately $6.8 trillion in Q3, was directed towards the ongoing ramp-up of our Pyeongtaek Line 3 facility, specifically focusing on advanced DRAM production. We're seeing strong early yields on our 1alpha nanometer DRAM technology, fueling further investment in capacity expansion to meet anticipated demand from the PC and data center sectors. Additionally, we continued to invest in Phase 2 of our Xi'an NAND flash memory fab, allocating roughly $2.1 trillion this quarter, which is crucial for capturing the growing demand for high-density storage solutions in the mobile and enterprise markets. For our foundry business, we invested $2.0 trillion in Q3 to support the ongoing construction of our new fabrication facilities in Austin and Taylor, Texas. While these facilities are not expected to come online until late 2024/early 2025, early investments are critical for ensuring timely completion and minimizing potential supply chain disruptions. We are already seeing significant interest from potential clients, particularly in the automotive and industrial sectors, seeking access to advanced process nodes. We project that the US plants will contribute a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion once fully operational, with a specific focus on 5nm and 3nm technologies. Approximately $600 billion was allocated to advanced packaging technologies, including 2.5D and 3D stacking solutions. Our Display division accounted for $0.5 trillion of our Q3 CapEx, bringing the year-to-date total to $2.1 trillion. A majority of the Display CapEx, approximately $350 billion, was focused on increasing production capacity and improving yields for both Quantum Dot OLED (QD-OLED) and White OLED (WOLED) technologies. We are seeing robust demand for our QD-OLED displays in the premium TV segment, and we are actively working to expand our production capacity to meet this demand. Furthermore, we are continuously refining our WOLED technology for use in IT products, such as laptops and tablets. We continue to invest in flexible OLED technology for mobile devices, allocating approximately $150 billion in Q3, aiming to develop new and innovative display form factors, such as foldable and rollable displays. Looking ahead to Q4 2023, we anticipate a slight moderation in CapEx spending, primarily due to the completion of several key projects in the DS division. We are carefully monitoring macroeconomic conditions and adjusting our investment plans accordingly to ensure that we are maximizing our return on investment. Due to rising inflation and supply chain constraints, we are actively evaluating cost optimization measures across all our CapEx projects. This includes renegotiating contracts with suppliers, optimizing construction timelines, and exploring alternative sourcing options. We are confident that these measures will help us mitigate the impact of inflation and ensure that we remain on track to achieve our financial goals. We expect our total CapEx for the next year to increase by roughly 7%.

Additionally, strong performance of premium smartphone models, including the Galaxy S24 series and the Z Fold/Flip line showed strong operating margin. Compared to Q3 2023, the operating margin is up 1.3 percentage points (from 12.8% to 14.1%). The most significant driver of the YoY improvement is the strong recovery in the semiconductor market. In Q3 2023, the memory chip market was in a severe downturn. The recovery in memory prices, particularly for DRAM, has contributed to a significant increase in operating profit in the DS division. YoY, we have seen a higher proportion of sales coming from our premium smartphone models, such as the Galaxy S24 series and the Z Fold/Flip series. This has led to higher average selling prices and improved profitability in the MX division. We have been implementing various cost optimization initiatives across the company, including streamlining our supply chain, improving manufacturing efficiency, and reducing overhead expenses. These efforts have contributed to a reduction in our cost of goods sold and operating expenses as a percentage of revenue.

Operating profit within the DS division declined by $2.5 trillion, largely due to increased capital expenditures, NAND flash pricing pressure, and DRAM demand softness. We accelerated our investment in EUV lithography equipment for the next-generation DRAM and NAND flash memory production lines. This strategic investment resulted in higher depreciation and amortization expenses, impacting operating profit by approximately $1.1 trillion. Despite a volume increase of 12% in NAND flash sales, average selling prices (ASPs) declined by 8% due to increased industry capacity and inventory correction among major cloud service providers. This pricing pressure eroded approximately $800 billion from operating profit. While DRAM demand from the PC segment showed signs of stabilization, demand from the mobile segment weakened slightly due to seasonal factors and inventory adjustments by key smartphone manufacturers. This resulted in a modest ASP decline of 2%, impacting operating profit by around $600 billion. The MX division also contributed to the overall decline, albeit to a lesser extent. Operating profit decreased by $500 billion QoQ, primarily due to higher marketing expenses and increased component costs, partially offset by a strong performance in the wearables category. The DP division showed a slight improvement in operating profit QoQ, contributing a small positive offset to the overall decline.

Now I’ll pass it to Michael Brown to provide color on execution.

Michael Brown, Chief Operating Officer:
Thanks, David.

From a delivery and operations standpoint, this was one of our more efficient quarters in recent memory.

A big part of that was the cost reduction initiatives, especially in advanced packaging and manufacturing process optimization, which allowed us to yield around $700 million in savings. This includes the successful ramp-up of our 1alpha DRAM node with improved cost efficiencies.

We also saw execution gains related to the strong performance of premium smartphone models, including the Galaxy S24 series and the Z Fold/Flip line, including a higher proportion of sales coming from our premium smartphone models, leading to higher average selling prices and improved profitability in the MX division.

Lastly, we began pilots tied to advanced packaging technologies, including 2.5D and 3D stacking solutions, where early signs are promising. As chip scaling becomes increasingly challenging, advanced packaging is playing a more critical role in enhancing performance and functionality. We are collaborating closely with key ecosystem partners to develop cutting-edge packaging solutions for high-performance computing and AI applications.

Now I’ll turn it over to Dr. Tanaka to discuss

Dr. Kenji Tanaka, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Michael.

On the technology side, our teams delivered important milestones across multiple streams.

First, we completed major feature work aligned with the revenue results, QoQ and YoY changes, and performance against guidance, especially in our System LSI division, driven primarily by the System-on-Chip (SoC) business. We project overall System LSI revenue to reach $5.8 billion in Q3, representing a 12% increase quarter-over-quarter (QoQ) and a 7% increase year-over-year (YoY). This growth is directly attributable to the anticipated success of the new flagship smartphone launch by our key tier-one Android partner. We forecast a 22% QoQ increase in SoC revenue, reaching $3.1 billion in Q3. We expect the strongest SoC demand to originate from North America and Europe, aligning with the projected sales distribution of our partner’s device. For the full year, we are revising our initial System LSI revenue growth forecast upward to 6%, reflecting the strong anticipated performance in Q3.

We also rolled out enhancements supporting the strong performance of premium smartphone models, including the Galaxy S24 series and the Z Fold/Flip line, including enhanced image sensors and battery life optimizations.

One final point — we’ve made structural improvements to better enable sales guidance, forecast, or trend by segment next quarter or full year for our Foundry business, including improved resource allocation, enhanced yield management, and strategic partnerships with equipment suppliers. These efforts have enabled us to increase our overall fab utilization rate to 95% in Q3. We are maintaining our full-year revenue growth forecast for the Foundry business at 25%, reflecting our confidence in our ability to capitalize on the long-term trends driving demand for advanced semiconductor manufacturing. We anticipate to be ready for 3nm mass production by Q4.

Let’s now open the floor for Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Thanks. You mentioned gains in net margin and diluted EPS. What gives you confidence that these are sustainable?

Dr. Anya Sharma:
We are focused on several key strategic initiatives to further improve our net margin and EPS, including continued investment in R&D (earmarking $5 trillion for the next fiscal year), supply chain optimization, and digital transformation.

Analyst 2:
On proactive cost-cutting measures, is this sustainable?

David Lee:
Yes, we are actively evaluating cost optimization measures across all our CapEx projects. This includes renegotiating contracts with suppliers, optimizing construction timelines, and exploring alternative sourcing options.

Analyst 3:
Can you elaborate on early traction with advanced packaging technologies?

Michael Brown:
We are collaborating closely with key ecosystem partners to develop cutting-edge packaging solutions for high-performance computing and AI applications. We are seeing strong interest and early adoption in these areas.

Analyst 4:
How are you thinking about long-term opportunity in sales guidance, forecast, or trend by segment next quarter or full year for our Foundry business?

Dr. Kenji Tanaka:
We are investing heavily in expanding our production capacity to meet future demand, including the construction of new fabs in the United States and South Korea. We anticipate to be ready for 3nm mass production by Q4.

Closing

Dr. Anya Sharma:
Thanks again to everyone for joining us. We’re energized by the results this quarter and remain focused on disciplined execution and strategic expansion. Looking forward to sharing continued progress next time.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes today’s call. You may now disconnect.
